source.title: A suite of Vision Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The study reports monosemanticity results for sparse-autoencoder features, not polysemanticity of individual neurons or any other behavior named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The Sort Eval result concerns SAE features, a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. The reported feature activation frequency and reconstruction MSE do not measure any claim version. Cited prior work is not recorded as a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The post releases residual-stream SAEs for a CLIP ViT and reports layer-wise SAE-feature monosemanticity (Sort Eval, no scores) and reconstruction MSE. It measures no individual neurons and never tests whether neurons are polysemantic, why, or how measurement affects that. Its subject is SAE features, a related but different construct. The relation is arguably 'cites_only' or 'discusses'; the post never even mentions polysemantic neurons, so T6 holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Preliminary, explicitly non-rigorous analysis suggests layer 20 is the most monosemantic and its features activate most frequently, so it is a reasonable alternative to the commonly used layer 22. The authors also report that outer patch tokens are easier to reconstruct than central ones.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains vision-transformer sparse autoencoders and evaluates their features; it does not apply the original neuron-analysis method.

fits_no_version.finding: Sort Eval autointerpretability suggests layer 20 is the most monosemantic SAE layer of the CLIP ViT-L; no scores are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpretability of residual-stream SAE features in vision transformers varies by layer.

record.problems: The authors characterize the analysis as preliminary and not demonstrated to a high degree of rigor. The text gives no quantitative Sort Eval scores or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: The reported layer-20 feature activation frequency and token reconstruction MSE are not measurements of neuron polysemanticity or any other claim version.
